name: Gutter Capital
identity_check: Confirmed as Gutter Capital (gutter.cc), the New York City early-stage VC firm Dan Teran (founder of Managed by Q) and James Gettinger founded in 2021; it runs the Elbow Grease accelerator (elbowgrease.cc / elbowgrease.gutter.cc). TechCrunch (Mar 2023) and the Fund I and Fund III PR Newswire releases all link gutter.cc and name the same founders. Not a gutter, roofing or home-services company despite the name.

thesis_text.value: Generalist pre-seed and seed firm in New York that leads rounds in software and AI-enabled companies run by mission-driven founders working on affordability, economic mobility and climate/sustainability (housing, healthcare, education, small business, emissions). Usually takes a board seat and works hands-on; runs Elbow Grease, an NYC accelerator. Avoids advertising, gaming, gambling, crypto and entertainment.

open_items: Fund II ($44M) close date and the funds' legal names not found; SEC EDGAR refused the declared User-Agent, so Form D filings were not checked; traded.co (Fund III article) returned 403. Fund close dates are announcement dates.
Company LinkedIn URL not recorded: gutter.cc does not link one. Partner LinkedIn URLs are not linked from the firm's site either.

Nothing found on investing in Indian founders. No stated US-entity requirement; the portfolio includes Germany-based The Climate Choice and Toronto-based Aerium, though Teran wrote they 'do not typically seek out European investments'. Elbow Grease asks founders to work in person at Gutter HQ on Canal Street, NYC.

No portfolio count is reported. gutter.cc/companies lists 26 companies (Fund I 10, Fund II 12, Fund III 4); TechCrunch (Mar 2023) said 13 investments in the prior year; the Fund III release says only that the firm is 'small by design, making few investments each year'.

application_url is the Elbow Grease accelerator page (batch 2 applications closed 2026-07-31; an interest form for the next batch is linked). The core fund has no form; founders are asked to email the firm (address not recorded).

Stated sectors combine the 2026 FAQ ('generalist ... software and AI enabled businesses') with the 2023 Fund I focus (SaaS and marketplaces in healthcare, housing, education, small business and climate). health_bio not added because healthcare is framed as an affordability theme.

Rounds not recorded because no fetched page naming Gutter in that round was found, or the page was blocked: QuickSecure seed (June 2026, database hints only), Soundtrace, BuildCasa (Gettinger's post says Gutter led the pre-seed in fall 2022, no amount; the later round sits on a 403 finsmes page), The Climate Choice seed (Gutter's post gives no amount or co-investors), Treehouse 2023 round (Gutter's post names Montage Ventures and Trucks VC as leads but not Gutter's role; Axios 403), Forerunner seed and $26.3M Series B (B says only 'all existing investors returning'), Bikky Series A, and Fund II companies Allera, Dewey, Faraday, FarmEvo, Parcell, Recharged, RetailPath, Roble and Upkid. The Business Wire Punch release timed out.

Elbow Grease batch 1 (Upstarts): Galileo Space, GRAIL, JoyWork, Keeper Systems, LegacyAI, Punch, QuickSecure, SwitchBoard, each on $300k/9% terms; only Keeper (its own news page) and Punch (a separate seed) are recorded as rounds.

Operating partners Richard Hughes (Head of Talent) and Vince Li (Head of Product), and operations lead Carli Casteel, not recorded as investing partners. Partner focus_sectors are classified from their writing (Teran: climate and housing posts, the AI accelerator; Gettinger: AI essay, housing posts); the firm assigns no sector coverage.
Forerunner Series A: date not disclosed (first made public 2026-02-05 with the Series B), so date left null. Aerium: SAFE closed July 2026, dated by its 2026-10-16 announcement.
